A01.title: Parsing problems
A01.diagnosis: The file was not parsed into clean rows and columns.

A02.title: Index saved as a column
A02.diagnosis: An old row index was saved into the file as a column.

A03.title: Duplicate columns
A03.diagnosis: Two columns have the same name or the same content.

A04.title: Duplicate rows
A04.diagnosis: Some rows are exact copies of other rows.

A05.title: Conflicting duplicates
A05.diagnosis: Rows with the same features have different target values.

A06.title: Almost empty rows
A06.diagnosis: Some rows have most of their cells missing.

A07.title: Problem column names
A07.diagnosis: Some column names have spaces, special characters or are empty.

params.reason: rename the column; the fix vocabulary has no rename action

B01.title: Numbers stored as text
B01.diagnosis: The column holds numbers stored as text.

B02.title: Dates stored as text
B02.diagnosis: The column holds dates stored as text.

B03.title: Mixed formats in one column
B03.diagnosis: The column mixes several value formats.

B04.title: Numeric code, may be categorical
B04.diagnosis: The numbers are codes, so their size and order have no meaning.

B05.title: Inconsistent category labels
B05.diagnosis: The same category is written in several ways.

B06.title: Mixed boolean tokens
B06.diagnosis: The column uses several token pairs for true and false.

B07.title: Numbers with units or suffixes
B07.diagnosis: The column holds numbers written with a unit or suffix (for example 1.37kg or 3.2k).

B08.title: Several values packed in one column
B08.diagnosis: Each value holds two or more numbers in a fixed text pattern (for example 3 bd / 2 ba).

B09.title: Mixed date formats
B09.diagnosis: The column writes dates in two or more formats.

C02.title: Hidden missing values
C02.diagnosis: Missing values are stored as text tokens.

C03.title: Sentinel numbers
C03.diagnosis: A special number is used in place of a missing or special value.

C04.title: Informative missingness
C04.diagnosis: Rows with a missing value have a different target than other rows.

C05.title: Co-missing block
C05.diagnosis: These columns are missing in the same rows, so they share one cause.

C06.title: Almost fully missing column
C06.diagnosis: Almost all values of the column are missing.

D01.title: Impossible values
D01.diagnosis: Some values are outside the possible range of the column.

D02.title: Extreme isolated values
D02.diagnosis: Some values are far from all other values, likely typos.

D03.title: Invalid dates
D03.diagnosis: Some dates are in the future or are placeholder dates.

D04.title: Cross-column rule violations
D04.diagnosis: A few rows break a rule that holds for almost all other rows.

D05.title: Rare categories
D05.diagnosis: Some categories have very few rows.

E01.title: Constant column
E01.diagnosis: The column has one value only, so it carries no information.

E02.title: Quasi-constant column
E02.diagnosis: Almost all rows have the same value.

E03.title: ID-like column
E03.diagnosis: The column is an identifier and must not be used as a feature.

E04.title: High-cardinality categorical
E04.diagnosis: The column has too many categories for one-hot encoding.

E05.title: Free text column
E05.diagnosis: The column holds free text, which this tool does not analyze.

E06.title: One-to-one categorical mapping
E06.diagnosis: Two columns map one to one, so one of them is redundant.

E07.title: Exact linear relation
E07.diagnosis: One column is an exact linear combination of others.

E08.title: Very high correlation
E08.diagnosis: Two columns carry almost the same information.

E09.title: Heavy skew
E09.diagnosis: The distribution has a long tail.

F01.title: Missing target
F01.diagnosis: Some rows have no target value and can not be used for training.

F02.title: Task type doubt
F02.diagnosis: The target values do not clearly fit the given task type.

F03.title: Inconsistent class labels
F03.diagnosis: The same class is written in several ways.

F04.title: Class imbalance
F04.diagnosis: One class is much more common than the others.

F05.title: Rare classes
F05.diagnosis: Some classes have very few rows; the target label space never changes, so this is reported only.

params.reason: the target label space never changes, so this is reported only

F06.title: Regression target shape
F06.diagnosis: The target is skewed or has zeros or negatives.

F07.title: Target outliers
F07.diagnosis: Some target values are far from the others; the target label space never changes, so this is reported only.

params.reason: the target label space never changes, so this is reported only

G01.title: Feature predicts the target almost perfectly
G01.diagnosis: One feature alone predicts the target, which suggests leakage.

G02.title: Categories map almost purely to one target value
G02.diagnosis: The categories of this column give away the target.

G03.title: Name suggests after-the-event information
G03.diagnosis: The column name suggests it is known only after the target event.

G04.title: Missingness predicts the target
G04.diagnosis: The column is missing almost only for one class.

H01.title: Repeated entities
H01.diagnosis: The same entity appears in several rows, so a random split leaks.

H02.title: Time structure
H02.diagnosis: The target changes over time, so a random split is too optimistic.

H03.title: Sorted file
H03.diagnosis: The rows are sorted, so they must be shuffled before splitting.

H04.title: Near-duplicate rows
H04.diagnosis: Some rows are almost equal and would leak across the split.

H05.title: Small dataset
H05.diagnosis: The dataset is small, so use cross-validation and simple models.

P01.title: Non-numeric columns left
P01.diagnosis: The model input still has non-numeric columns.

P02.title: NaN or infinite values
P02.diagnosis: The model input still has NaN or infinite values.

P03.title: New constant columns
P03.diagnosis: A processing step created constant columns.

P05.title: Train/test schema mismatch
P05.diagnosis: Train and test data have different columns, order or types.
